notes: Fix: the carrier's screw-terminal ports (VIN, GND, M1+..M4-) were kind 'lug', which does not pair with a lead. They are now kind 'header-socket', because a bare lead or wire end is clamped into each terminal, and lead into header-socket is a compatible join. The connections are unchanged.
MKR Motor Carrier is not in the catalogue (lookup_part only found the different MKR Connector Carrier), so a new type was drafted.

The MKR family board is unspecified; the image resembles a MKR WiFi 1010, so arduino-mkr1000-wifi was used. It plugs into the carrier's MKR socket via its header pins, so the edge to the board has no board-side port.
The 3S LiPo battery's leads go to the VIN/GND terminal block on the carrier (screw terminals); no jumper wires or breadboard are used.
The optional DC motor is wired to M1+/M1- as in the circuit image; its leads are symmetric, so lead 1 to M1+ is arbitrary.
The carrier's ON/OFF switch is not modelled as a part; the tutorial says to flick it to ON.
The optional power supply is an alternative to the battery and is not included.
